title: CRLF normalization uses awkward split_last with dead fallback
description:
mime-tree/src/header_typed.rs:213-236 — the LF→CRLF normalization branch is written as raw_value.split_last().map(|(_, head)| { ... build vec ... }).unwrap_or_else(|| b"
".to_vec()). The split_last() can only return None if raw_value is empty, but the enclosing else-if already verified raw_value.ends_with(b"
"), which implies non-empty. The unwrap_or_else branch is dead code. Idiomatic rewrite: let head = &raw_value[..raw_value.len() - 1]; let mut v = Vec::with_capacity(head.len() + 2); v.extend_from_slice(head); v.extend_from_slice(b"
"); — or factor the whole if/else if/else block into a helper returning Cow<'_, [u8]>. The current shape signals 'I do not trust the invariant I just verified' which is the kind of pattern reviewers wince at.
close_reason: Code cleanup batch: (.3) removed dead 'year != 0' guard in date arm and replaced comment with accurate description of what month/day == 0 catches (year mapping in mail-parser-0.11 means parts[2] is never 0 after remap); (.21) eliminated unreachable! by folding Raw and URLs handling into the same outer match as the other forms — no top-level if-and-then-match anymore; (.22) replaced split_last + unwrap_or_else with straightforward slice arithmetic via a new crlf_terminated helper returning Cow; (.23) extracted trim_or_none helper for the RFC 8621 §4.1.2.3/§4.1.2.4 display-name normalisation rule, called from both convert_addr and group_addresses.
